title: Photonic operator storage/computation frontier (ideal simulation only)
hypothesis: For multiple useful 4x4 unitary tasks sharing a fixed Hadamard optical core, output/input phase Views preserve exact operator quality at lower serialized payload bytes than independent dense operators; native phase-bank controls will determine whether any Mirror-specific advantage remains.
scope: Deterministic ideal linear-optics simulation; not a LightPro/MZI device measurement.
tasks: Eight independent phase-coded transformations per world, target U_t = D_out(phi_t) H D_in(psi_t), with 4 channels and phases sampled uniformly in [-pi,pi].
controls: one shared H operator for all tasks
metrics: max output error on fixed probe vectors
simulated complex MAC and phase operation counts

storage.authority: actual serialized torch.save inference payload bytes including shared core, task phases, dense matrices, routing/task metadata, and object descriptions
paid_objects: Hadamard matrix or dense task matrices

compute: Count 4x4 complex MACs and scalar phase modulators in ideal algebra only; no timing, joules, thermal tuning, insertion loss, fabrication footprint, or switch latency inferred.
success_gate: At least 7/8 tasks per fresh world have relative operator error <=1e-6 and factorized payload <=50% of dense independent payload.
failure_gate: Any fresh world fails quality/byte gate, or Mirror exactly aliases a native direct phase bank with no measured Mirror-specific advantage.
post_run_audit: Native and Mirror payloads used different field names and metadata strings, producing a 64 B archive-size difference despite identical phase tensor values/shapes/dtypes. This confounds Mirror byte attribution. Fresh worlds were already opened; no same-ID rerun.
boundaries: Simulated operation counts are not measured energy/latency/footprint.
No physical device superiority claim absent LightPro/MZI hardware and calibrated measurements.
